record.original_question: A null 2-type submanifold is one whose mean curvature vector satisfies ΔH = cH for some nonzero constant c. Does every null 2-type surface in Euclidean 4-space E^4 have constant mean curvature?

evidence.quote: From the definition of null 2-type submanifolds and formula (1.3), it follows that the mean curvature vector H of a null 2-type submanifold satisfies the following simple condition: ΔH = cH, for some non-zero constant c.
The author doesn’t know whether every null 2-type surface in a Euclidean 4-space has constant mean curvature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth orientable surface immersed in Euclidean 4-space $\mathbb{E}^4$, with mean curvature vector field $H$ (a normal vector field on $M$) and Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ acting componentwise on vector-valued functions via the induced metric. The surface $M$ is said to be of null 2-type if there exists a nonzero real constant $c$ such that
$$\Delta H = c\, H,$$
and $M$ is not of 1-type (equivalently, $H$ is not an eigenvector of $\Delta$ corresponding to a single eigenvalue arising from the position vector decomposition; more concretely, the position vector of $M$ in $\mathbb{E}^4$ admits a decomposition $x = x_0 + x_1$ with $x_0$ a constant vector and $\Delta x_1 = \lambda x_1$ failing — instead one has a two-component decomposition with one harmonic component).

Question: Must every null 2-type surface in $\mathbb{E}^4$ have constant mean curvature, i.e., must $\|H\|$ be a constant function on $M$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up related results — null 2-type surfaces in $\mathbb{E}^3$ are known to be circular cylinders (Chen, 1988), null 2-type Chen surfaces have been studied (Li, 1994), and δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean spaces are known to have constant mean curvature — but no source was found establishing or refuting the general claim that every null 2-type surface in $\mathbb{E}^4$ has constant mean curvature. The status appears to remain unresolved in the general case.

status_evidence.title: Null 2-type surfaces in E^3 are circular cylinders
status_evidence.snippet: Chen (1988) classifies null 2-type surfaces in E^3 as circular cylinders, which have constant mean curvature.
status_evidence.claim: In E^3 the analogous statement holds; the E^4 case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurface in a Euclidean space has constant mean curvature and constant scalar curvature.
status_evidence.claim: A partial result for special null 2-type hypersurfaces, not the full E^4 surface case.

status_evidence.title: Null 2-type Chen surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies null 2-type surfaces under the Chen-surface assumption.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification under additional hypotheses; general E^4 case not settled.
